o1.biggest_strength: Every branch is finished — the six reason labels, the offer card, the done screen and the email confirmation — plus logging and a 10% holdout, so the product team can build it next sprint without another meeting.
o1.biggest_mistake: It keeps a speculative 50% discount for switchers with no test behind it and then books that group at £607 'after discount' when 67 subscribers at half price is about £300, and it gives no honest range as I asked.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cut or properly price the switcher discount and add a low-to-high range on kept subscribers and revenue, each end tied to a stated basis.

o2.biggest_strength: It leads with the decision and the billing blocker, puts 'rebuild the pause this week' first, and backs the headline with a +930 to +2,740 range and a clean reason-by-reason table that matches my splits exactly.
o2.biggest_mistake: It never says what a pauser, a plan switcher or a reminder-setter sees after they accept — the single done screen reads 'Your subscription is cancelled', which would tell a paused learner they cancelled — and the top of its range doesn't follow from its own 34%-accept assumption.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Write the done screen and confirmation email for each accepted offer, spell out the six reason labels, and tie the high end of the range to the stated accept rate.

reason: Output 1 is the one my team could build as written, because the states that matter most — pause, switch, reminder — all have a done screen and email, where Output 2 leaves the biggest lever (the pause) with a confirmation that says the learner has cancelled. Output 2 is the cleaner read and the honest range I asked for, but it hands back homework at exactly the point the build starts.
